sections.title: Property Sheet — PROP-G (Gail's house)
sections.md:
| # | Field | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Type and era | 1960s pebble-dashed semi-detached, decorated in the 1990s and kept since |
| 2 | Shell | pale duck-egg blue painted woodchip · plain bullnose pine skirting ~12 cm, honey varnish · matching pine architraves · flush sapele-veneer doors, brushed aluminium levers · white ceiling, paper lantern shade · moss-green twist carpet through hall, stairs, landing and bedrooms → beige vinyl at the kitchen (aluminium strip) · white double-panel convectors · square white switches, scuffed |
| 3 | Floor map | front door → hall; a single straight flight rises away from the door along the **right-hand** wall; the front room through the doorway on the **left**; the front bedroom at the top of the stairs, turning left on the landing |
| 4 | Orientation | the front (door glass, landing window, front bedroom) faces **south**: bright late morning, sun in by midday |
| 5 | Carried elements | the moss-green carpet · the pine handrail on white square spindles · the barometer · the walking stick in the umbrella stand |
| 6 | Exterior | pebble-dash front, a short concrete path to a low gate, a privet hedge; the semi opposite across the road |
| 7 | Standing negatives | none yet (first plate) |

sections.title: Light plans (§30K) — in room terms
sections.md:
| Location | Sources | Sun path | Key by time | Fill |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L-G-BED | the window on the south wall (camera-right from the door) | direct sun from ~11:00 | G-D1 late morning: bright but cool, angled across the quilt · G-D2 midday: sun on the floor, warmer | pale blue walls |
| L-G-HALL | front-door glass (south) + landing window (south, top of the stairs) | door glass sunlit from late morning | G-D1: the door-glass wash, grey · G-D2: a sun patch on the carpet | the pale walls, the stair carpet |
| L-N-WORK | the sash window, east wall (camera-left from the door) | morning sun | N-D1 morning: soft, warm on the brick | red brick, the runner |
| L-K-STOP | open sky, brighter to the south | overcast K-D1 · broken cloud K-D2 | K-D1 morning: flat, cool · K-D2 afternoon: brighter, warmer | pavement bounce |
| L-J-LOUNGE | the window, west wall, net curtains (camera-left from the door) | afternoon sun on the curtains | J-D1 afternoon: grey, even through the nets | magnolia walls |
| L-J-STEPS | open sky over a north-facing street | low west sun in the afternoon | J-D1: overcast, cool · J-D2: low warm sun raking across the steps | the sandstone |
| L-CONSULT | the window on the right-hand wall, the X-ray screen, a ceiling panel | — | overcast daylight, flat panel on | pale green walls |

**Light arc (Mode 1, daylight only):** Hooks and Acts 1–3 are the **problem**: grey, flatter, cooler daylight (G-D1, K-D1, J-D1). Act 4 is the **turn** and moves to G-D2 at the product. Acts 5–6 are the **after**: sun in the room, warmer, windows open (G-D2, K-D2, J-D2). Never dark, never moody (§12).
